text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Local council polls to go ahead as planned on March 15, national council of state grouping top brass of military government and state governors decides after two days of talks in capital Abuja.

- Indigenous oil firm Amni International Petroleum Development Company last weekend exported 630,000 barrels of crude oil from its field, becoming third local firm to go into oil production and export business.
- Nigeria says it bent over backwards to accomodate demands of two U.N. human rights investigators who have cancelled planned visit to the country.
- Dunlop reopens for business; 22 of its workers are charged with rioting which forced its closure on Tuesday.
- Air force begins preliminary investigations into Monday crash of one of its Dornier Sky Servant plane in the north; two pilots and technician on board died.
- Radical opposition lawyers Gani Fawehinmi and Femi Falana volunteer to take over free of charge legal defence of detained presidential claimant Moshood Abiola.
- Jamaican ambassador to Nigeria Robert Milla says his family has lost all its property in a fire that gutted his Lagos residence on Saturday while they were out of town.

- Savannah Bank plans to raise its capital base to 600 million naira from a current 53 million naira in order to meet new official requirement that banks should shore up capital bases to a minimum of 500 million naira, a nine-fold increase.
- New decree says all contracts not executed since General Sani Abacha seized power in November 1993 are to be probed and those responsible for the failure will face a tribunal.
- Police say bombs that have rocked Lagos in recent months were locally made.
- Political parties conclude nominations of candidates for local council elections
- President of the Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Kola Daisi,says Economic Community of West African States sub-region should become a truly free trade area
